issues.description: The Person.id attribute type is inconsistent across artifacts: the problem statement and the template repository define Person.id as UUID, and the server-side resources and services expect UUID (e.g., PersonService uses UUID.randomUUID(), PersonResource uses UUID path variables). However, the solution repository's common Person model uses Long for the id field. This mismatch is a structural inconsistency that would prevent the code from compiling and confuses students about the correct id type to use when implementing endpoints and client interactions.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the Person.id type consistent across all artifacts. Preferably revert the solution repository's common Person model to use UUID for the id (matching the problem statement, template, and server code). Concretely: change the id field type in solution_repository/src/common/java/de/tum/in/ase/eist/model/Person.java from Long to java.util.UUID, update its getter/setter signatures accordingly, and ensure all usages compile. Alternatively, if Long is intended, update server-side PersonService and PersonResource to use Long consistently (including id generation and path variable types) and update the problem statement/template to document Long instead of UUID.

issues.description: The conceptual entity 'Person.id' is inconsistent across artifacts: the problem statement and the template define the person's identifier as a UUID, and the server-side service and resource code expect/handle UUIDs, but the solution's common Person model declares the id as a Long. This type/name mismatch for the identifier breaks the conceptual mapping (what a "Person id" is) and will confuse students trying to map the problem requirements (which reference UUID personId) to the provided solution code.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the Person.id representation consistent across all artifacts. Prefer aligning the solution model with the problem/template by changing solution_repository/src/common/java/de/tum/in/ase/eist/model/Person.java to use UUID for the id (UUID getId()/setId(UUID)), or alternatively change the server/service/resource code and the problem text to use Long consistently. The least confusing correction is to use UUID everywhere (update the solution's Person class to declare id as java.util.UUID).
